In the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, Sempra’s depreciation and amortization decreased by $30 million (5%) to $632 million primarily due to:

▪ $65 million lower at Sempra Infrastructure as a result of classifying SI Partners as held for sale in September 2025

▪ $38 million higher at Sempra California due to higher utility plant rate base

In the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, Sempra’s depreciation and amortization decreased by $90 million (5%) to $1.9 billion primarily due to:

▪ $213 million lower at Sempra Infrastructure as a result of classifying SI Partners and Ecogas as held for sale in September 2025 and June 2025, respectively

▪ $126 million higher at Sempra California due to higher utility plant rate base

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
In the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, Sempra’s interest expense decreased by $105 million (26%) to $298 million primarily due to:

▪ $130 million at Sempra Infrastructure primarily from:

◦ $117 million from $113 million unrealized gains in 2026 compared to $4 million unrealized losses in 2025 on interest rate swaps related to the PA LNG Phase 1 project

◦ $16 million interest expense in 2025 related to a customer’s early termination of firm transportation agreements

▪ $16 million at Sempra California from higher debt balances from debt issuances

▪ $9 million at Parent and other from higher debt balances from debt issuances and higher borrowings on commercial paper offset by higher capitalization of interest expense from projects under construction at Sempra Infrastructure

In the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, Sempra’s interest expense decreased by $85 million (7%) to $1.1 billion primarily due to:

▪ $201 million at Sempra Infrastructure from:

◦ $203 million favorable impact in interest expense from interest rate swaps related to the PA LNG Phase 1 project comprised of:

• $119 million from $59 million unrealized gains in 2026 compared to $60 million unrealized losses in 2025

• $84 million realized gains in 2026 from the termination of interest rate swaps, net of transaction costs

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
(1) We discuss how we recognize equity earnings in Note 5 of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in the Annual Report.

We report as part of our pretax results the income or loss attributable to NCI. However, we do not record income taxes for a portion of this income or loss, as some of our entities with NCI are currently treated as partnerships for U.S. income tax purposes, and thus we are only liable for income taxes on the portion of the earnings that are allocated to us. Our pretax income, however, includes 100% of these entities.

◦ $153 million income tax expense in 2025 for changes in state income tax apportionment

intro.text: We are a holding company whose principal businesses are regulated utilities in California and Texas. Our businesses invest in and operate electric and gas utilities and other energy infrastructure that provide energy services to customers. Sempra was formed in 1998 through a business combination of Enova Corporation and Pacific Enterprises, the holding companies of our regulated public utilities in California: SDG&E, which began operations in 1881, and SoCalGas, which began operations in 1867. We have since expanded our regulated public utility presence into Texas through our 80.25% interest in Oncor and 50% interest in Sharyland Utilities. Sempra Infrastructure’s assets include investments in the U.S. and Mexico with a focus on LNG, energy networks and low carbon solutions.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
